```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(citoMove)
library(terra)
library(amt)
```

## Overview

This appendix documents the four user-facing functions developed as part of this thesis and integrated into `citoMove`: `simulateTrack()`, `createRandomSteps()`, `extractStepCovariates()`, and `extractStepImagekernels()`. Together they form the pipeline used throughout the Methods and Results sections and in Appendices B-D: simulating a movement track under known habitat preferences (`simulateTrack()`), generating random/control steps around an observed track (`createRandomSteps()`), and attaching habitat covariate values to every step, either as scalar values for DNN-SSF (`extractStepCovariates()`) or as raw image kernels for CNN-SSF (`extractStepImagekernels()`).

For each function, this appendix gives a description of its purpose, an overview of its arguments and return value, and its full source code as implemented in the package. Internal helper routines that are only ever used inside one of these four functions (e.g. raster cropping/scaling, kernel extraction, the Random-Forest/MCMC density estimator used by `createRandomSteps()`) are defined as local functions at the top of the respective function body rather than as separate exported functions, and are documented inline in the source code shown below.

\newpage

## `simulateTrack()`

**Description.** Generates a simulated animal track using the Step Selection Function (SSF) method. At each step, a set of candidate steps is drawn from movement distributions (gamma for step length, von Mises for turning angle). Each candidate is evaluated using a habitat preference score derived from numeric and/or image raster layers, weighted by their respective beta coefficients. The next location is chosen via a softmax (conditional logit) draw over the candidates, so that selection probability increases exponentially with habitat score. All layers are cropped to their shared spatial overlap before simulation, and movement uses toroidal boundary conditions (the landscape wraps around at its edges).

**Arguments.**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `xStart`, `yStart` | Starting coordinates of the animal. |
| `crs` | Coordinate reference system of the starting coordinates. |
| `tStart`, `timeStep` | Starting timestamp and time elapsed per step. |
| `angleStart` | Starting direction of movement (degrees from north). |
| `nSteps` | Number of steps to simulate. |
| `nChoiceSet` | Number of candidate steps drawn at each step. |
| `scaleSL`, `shapeSL` | Scale/shape parameters of the gamma step-length distribution. |
| `kappaTA` | Concentration parameter of the von Mises turning-angle distribution. |
| `numericLayers`, `betas` | Numeric habitat covariate layers and their preference coefficients. |
| `imageLayers`, `imageBetas` | Image-like habitat covariate layers and their preference coefficients. |
| `imageKernelDimensions`, `imageKernelFunctions` | Kernel size and aggregation function per image layer. |
| `scaleNumericLayers`, `scaleImageLayers` | Whether to rescale layers to (0, 1) before simulation. |

**Value.** An `amt` track object (class `track_xy`) with columns `x_`, `y_`, and `t_`.

```{r simulateTrack-source, eval = FALSE}
simulateTrack <- function(xStart = 0,
                          yStart = 0,
                          crs = NULL,
                          tStart = as.POSIXct("2026-01-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC"),
                          timeStep = "hour",
                          angleStart = 0,
                          nSteps = 100,
                          nChoiceSet = 100,
                          scaleSL = 2,
                          shapeSL = 2,
                          kappaTA = 2,
                          numericLayers = NULL,
                          betas = c(-3),
                          imageLayers = NULL,
                          imageKernelDimensions = c(3),
                          imageKernelFunctions = list(f1 = mean),
                          imageBetas = c(3),
                          scaleNumericLayers = TRUE,
                          scaleImageLayers = TRUE)
{

# Internal helper functions -------------------------------------------------
# These three functions are only ever needed inside simulateTrack(), so they
# are defined here as local functions instead of being exported separately.
# Being defined inside simulateTrack() means: they only exist while
# simulateTrack() is running, and they can "see" the arguments of
# simulateTrack() (e.g. imageKernelFunctions) without these having to be
# passed in explicitly every time.

  # Crops a raster layer to a given extent and optionally rescales it to (0, 1).
  # Used once per layer, right after the shared overlap extent of all layers
  # has been determined below.
  #   layer - SpatRaster to process
  #   ext   - SpatExtent to crop to (the shared overlap extent, see below)
  #   scale - if TRUE, rescale cropped values to (0, 1); skipped if the layer
  #           is constant (min == max), since dividing by zero would occur
  cropScaleRaster <- function(layer, ext, scale = TRUE) {
    r <- terra::crop(layer, ext)
    terra::ext(r) <- ext
    if (scale) {
      r_min <- terra::global(r, "min", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
      r_max <- terra::global(r, "max", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
      if (r_max > r_min) r <- (r - r_min) / (r_max - r_min)
    }
    r
  }

  # For each coordinate pair (xs[i], ys[i]), extracts the raster values inside
  # a square window of kernelDim x kernelDim pixels centred on that point and
  # aggregates them with kernelFun (e.g. mean, max). This is how an "image"
  # covariate contributes information from a neighbourhood of pixels rather
  # than from a single point. Raster borders are wrapped toroidally, i.e. a
  # window that runs off one edge of the raster continues on the opposite
  # edge (consistent with the toroidal boundary conditions used for movement
  # in the simulation loop below).
  #   raster    - SpatRaster to read from
  #   xs, ys    - coordinates of the query points (same length)
  #   kernelDim - odd side length (in pixels) of the square window
  #   kernelFun - aggregation function applied to the values in each window
  extractKernelValues <- function(raster, xs, ys, kernelDim, kernelFun) {
    res_x <- terra::res(raster)[1]
    res_y <- terra::res(raster)[2]
    half  <- floor(kernelDim / 2)

    border  <- terra::ext(raster)
    x_range <- border[2] - border[1]
    y_range <- border[4] - border[3]

    offsets <- expand.grid(dx = seq(-half, half),
                           dy = seq(-half, half))
    n_pts <- length(xs)
    n_off <- nrow(offsets)

    all_x <- rep(xs, each = n_off) +
      rep(offsets$dx, times = n_pts) * res_x
    all_y <- rep(ys, each = n_off) +
      rep(offsets$dy, times = n_pts) * res_y

    all_x <- ((all_x - border[1]) %% x_range) + border[1]
    all_y <- ((all_y - border[3]) %% y_range) + border[3]

    vals_all <- terra::extract(raster, cbind(all_x, all_y))[, 1]
    vals_mat <- matrix(vals_all, nrow = n_pts,
                       ncol = n_off, byrow = TRUE)

    apply(vals_mat, 1, function(row) {
      v <- row[!is.na(row)]
      if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else kernelFun(v)
    })
  }

  # Loops extractKernelValues() over all image layers, multiplies each
  # resulting kernel value with its corresponding beta coefficient and sums
  # everything up. Returns a single "image habitat score" per query point,
  # combining the contribution of every image layer at once. Returns a
  # vector of zeros if no image layers were supplied, so it can always be
  # added to the numeric-layer contribution without an extra if-check at the
  # call site.
  #   x, y                   - coordinates of the query points
  #   imageRasters           - list of already cropped (and scaled) image SpatRasters
  #   imageBetas             - preference coefficient per image layer
  #   imageKernelDimensions  - kernel side length per image layer
  #   imageKernelFunctions   - aggregation function per image layer
  computeImageValues <- function(x, y,
                                  imageRasters,
                                  imageBetas,
                                  imageKernelDimensions,
                                  imageKernelFunctions) {
    if (length(imageRasters) == 0) return(rep(0, length(x)))
    Reduce("+", lapply(seq_along(imageRasters), function(k) {
      imageBetas[[k]] * extractKernelValues(
        imageRasters[[k]], x, y,
        imageKernelDimensions[k],
        imageKernelFunctions[[k]]
      )
    }))
  }


# Validation:
  rasterList <- c(terra::as.list(numericLayers), terra::as.list(imageLayers))
  if (!inherits(tStart, "POSIXct") || length(tStart) != 1) stop("tStart must be a single value of class 'POSIXct'")
  if (!(is.numeric(timeStep) || timeStep %in% c("sec", "min", "hour", "day", "week", "month", "quarter", "year")) || length(timeStep) != 1)
    stop("timeStep must be a single numeric value or one of: sec, min, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year")
  if (!is.numeric(angleStart) || length(angleStart) != 1 || angleStart >= 360 || angleStart < 0) stop("angleStart must be a single positive number between 0 and 360")
  if (!is.numeric(nSteps) || length(nSteps) != 1 || nSteps != floor(nSteps) || nSteps <= 0) stop("nSteps must be a single positive integer")
  if (!is.numeric(nChoiceSet) || length(nChoiceSet) != 1 || nChoiceSet != floor(nChoiceSet) || nChoiceSet <= 0) stop("nChoiceSet must be a single positive integer")
  if (!is.numeric(scaleSL) || length(scaleSL) != 1 || scaleSL <= 0) stop("scaleSL must be a single positive number")
  if (!is.numeric(shapeSL) || length(shapeSL) != 1 || shapeSL <= 0) stop("shapeSL must be a single positive number")
  if (!is.numeric(kappaTA) || length(kappaTA) != 1 || kappaTA < 0) stop("kappaTA must be a single non-negative number")
  if (length(rasterList) == 0) stop("at least one layer must be provided")
  if (length(rasterList) > 1) {
    crsList  <- sapply(rasterList, terra::crs)
    nonEmpty <- crsList[nchar(crsList) > 0]
    if (length(nonEmpty) > 1 && length(unique(nonEmpty)) > 1)
      stop("All layers must have the same CRS")
  }
  if (!is.null(crs)) {
    crs_input <- if (is.numeric(crs)) paste0("EPSG:", crs) else crs
    crs_check <- tryCatch(terra::crs(crs_input), error = function(e) "")
    if (nchar(crs_check) == 0) stop("crs must be NULL or a valid coordinate reference system")
    layerCRS <- sapply(rasterList, terra::crs)
    layerCRS <- layerCRS[nchar(layerCRS) > 0]
    if (length(layerCRS) > 0 && !all(sapply(layerCRS, terra::same.crs, crs_input)))
      stop("crs must match the CRS of numericLayers and imageLayers")
  }
  if (!is.null(numericLayers)) {
    if (!inherits(numericLayers, "SpatRasterCollection")) stop("numericLayers must be of class 'SpatRasterCollection'")
    if (length(betas) != length(terra::as.list(numericLayers))) stop("betas must have one entry per numericLayer")
  }
  if (!is.null(imageLayers)) {
    nImageLayers <- length(terra::as.list(imageLayers))
    if (!inherits(imageLayers, "SpatRasterCollection")) stop("imageLayers must be of class 'SpatRasterCollection'")
    if (length(imageKernelDimensions) != nImageLayers) stop("imageKernelDimensions must have one entry per imageLayer")
    if (length(imageKernelFunctions) != nImageLayers) stop("imageKernelFunctions must have one entry per imageLayer")
    if (length(imageBetas) != nImageLayers) stop("imageBetas must have one entry per imageLayer")
    if (any(imageKernelDimensions %% 2 == 0)) stop("All imageKernelDimensions must be odd numbers")
  }


# Setting up numericLayer Rasters: (cutting to overlap size)
  xminAll <- max(sapply(rasterList, function(l) terra::ext(l)[1]))
  xmaxAll <- min(sapply(rasterList, function(l) terra::ext(l)[2]))
  yminAll <- max(sapply(rasterList, function(l) terra::ext(l)[3]))
  ymaxAll <- min(sapply(rasterList, function(l) terra::ext(l)[4]))
  extAll  <- terra::ext(xminAll, xmaxAll, yminAll, ymaxAll)
  rasters <- lapply(rasterList, function(l) terra::crop(l, extAll))
  if (xStart < extAll[1] || xStart > extAll[2] || yStart < extAll[3] || yStart > extAll[4]) stop("Starting coordinates must be inside of overlaping layer extend")
  if (xminAll >= xmaxAll || yminAll >= ymaxAll) stop("The provided layers must have a spatial overlap")

# Adding image and numeric Layers if present: (cutting to size and scaling)
  imageRasters <- if (!is.null(imageLayers)) {
    lapply(terra::as.list(imageLayers),
           cropScaleRaster, ext = extAll,
           scale = scaleImageLayers)
  } else list()

  numericRasters <- if (!is.null(numericLayers)) {
    lapply(terra::as.list(numericLayers),
           cropScaleRaster, ext = extAll,
           scale = scaleNumericLayers)
  } else list()

# Initializing tibble and starting point:
  simData <- tibble::tibble(stepID    = 0:nSteps,
                            x_        = numeric(nSteps + 1),
                            y_        = numeric(nSteps + 1),
                            SL        = numeric(nSteps + 1),
                            Direction = numeric(nSteps + 1),
                            Change    = numeric(nSteps + 1),
                            habitat   = numeric(nSteps + 1))
  simData$x_[1] <- xStart
  simData$y_[1] <- yStart
  simData$SL[1] <- 0
  simData$Direction[1] <- angleStart
  simData$Change[1] <- 0

  numVal_start <- if (length(numericRasters) == 0) 0 else
    Reduce("+", lapply(seq_along(numericRasters), function(k)
      betas[[k]] * terra::extract(numericRasters[[k]], cbind(simData$x_[1], simData$y_[1]))[, 1]))

  imgVal_start <- computeImageValues(simData$x_[1],
                                     simData$y_[1],
                                     imageRasters,
                                     imageBetas,
                                     imageKernelDimensions,
                                     imageKernelFunctions)
  simData$habitat[1] <- numVal_start + imgVal_start

# Simulation loop:
  for (i in 1:nSteps) {
    SLrel     <- stats::rgamma(nChoiceSet, shape = shapeSL, scale = scaleSL)
    ChangeRad <- circular::rvonmises(nChoiceSet, mu = circular::circular(0), kappa = kappaTA)
    Change    <- as.numeric(ChangeRad) * 180 / pi
    TArel     <- simData$Direction[i] + Change
    x         <- simData$x_[i] + SLrel * sin(TArel * pi / 180)
    y         <- simData$y_[i] + SLrel * cos(TArel * pi / 180)
    border    <- terra::ext(rasters[[1]])
    xToro     <- ((x - border[1]) %% (border[2] - border[1])) + border[1]
    yToro     <- ((y - border[3]) %% (border[4] - border[3])) + border[3]
    Direction <- (atan2(x - simData$x_[i], y - simData$y_[i]) * 180 / pi) %% 360

    numLinpred <- if (length(numericRasters) == 0) {
      rep(0, nChoiceSet)
    } else {
      Reduce("+", lapply(seq_along(numericRasters), function(k)
        betas[[k]] * terra::extract(numericRasters[[k]], cbind(xToro, yToro))[, 1]))
    }

    imgLinpred <- computeImageValues(xToro,
                                     yToro,
                                     imageRasters,
                                     imageBetas,
                                     imageKernelDimensions,
                                     imageKernelFunctions)
    linpred    <- numLinpred + imgLinpred

    rawLinpred <- linpred
    linpred    <- linpred - max(linpred)
    p          <- exp(linpred) / sum(exp(linpred))
    multinom   <- stats::rmultinom(1, size = 1, prob = p)
    chosenStep <- which(multinom == 1)

    simData$x_[i + 1]        <- x[chosenStep]
    simData$y_[i + 1]        <- y[chosenStep]
    simData$SL[i + 1]        <- SLrel[chosenStep]
    simData$Direction[i + 1] <- Direction[chosenStep]
    simData$Change[i + 1]    <- Change[chosenStep]
    simData$habitat[i+1]     <- rawLinpred[chosenStep]

    if (i %% 1000 == 0) message("Step ", i, "/", nSteps)
  }

# Adding timestamp:
  simData$t_ <- seq(from = tStart, by = timeStep, length.out = nrow(simData))
  x_ = y_ = t_ = NULL

  track <- amt::make_track(simData, x_, y_, t_, crs = if (is.null(crs)) NA else crs)
  return(track)
}
```

## `createRandomSteps()`

**Description.** Adds random (control) steps to a track or steps object, using one of three movement-kernel estimators: `"traditional"` (independent gamma step-length and von Mises turning-angle distributions, via `amt::random_steps()`), `"density"` (a bivariate kernel density estimate on step length and turning angle jointly, via `ks::kde()`, preserving their correlation), or `"density_advanced"` (a Random-Forest-based density surface combined with MCMC sampling via `BayesianTools`, which additionally avoids the KDE's tendency to force the density to zero at the domain edges). Every observed step is paired with `n_control` random alternatives sharing the same `step_id_`, and each step (observed and random) is assigned a `probability` value under the fitted movement kernel, which downstream models use as an importance-sampling correction (`offset(log(probability))` for iSSF, or the `density`/`weights` argument for `cnn_ssf()`/`dnn_ssf()`).

**Arguments.**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | An `amt` object of class `steps_xy`/`steps_xyt` or `track_xy`/`track_xyt`. |
| `estimator` | `"density"`, `"traditional"`, or `"density_advanced"`. |
| `n_control` | Number of random steps generated per observed step. |
| `rf_ntree`, `rf_n_bins`, `sl_transform`, `mcmc_burn_in` | Only used for `estimator = "density_advanced"`; control the Random Forest fit and the MCMC sampler. |

**Value.** An object of class `random_steps_prop` (inheriting from `random_steps`), containing `n_control` random alternatives per observed step and a `probability` column.

```{r createRandomSteps-source, eval = FALSE}
createRandomSteps <- function(x,
                              estimator    = c("density", "traditional", "density_advanced"),
                              n_control    = 10,
                              rf_ntree     = 500,
                              rf_n_bins    = 30,
                              sl_transform = c("none", "log1p"),
                              mcmc_burn_in = 1000) {

# Internal helper functions ---------------------------------------------
# All four helpers below are only ever needed for estimator =
# "density_advanced" (further down in this function) and nowhere else in
# the package, so they are defined here as local functions instead of
# being separate top-level functions. Being defined inside
# createRandomSteps() means: they only exist while createRandomSteps() is
# running, and bayesianToolsSampleDensitySurface() can call
# evalDensitySurfaceRF() directly (as a "sibling" function defined in the
# same enclosing function) without it having to be passed in as an argument.

  # Fit a 2D density surface using a random forest.
  #
  # Bins die beobachteten (sl, ta)-Paare in ein Gitter und trainiert einen
  # Random Forest, der die Haeufigkeits-"Landschaft" ueber dem (sl, ta)-Raum
  # vorhersagt. Im Gegensatz zur KDE wird die Flaeche an den Raendern nicht
  # kuenstlich auf 0 gezwungen, sondern aus den Nachbar-Bins interpoliert.
  #
  #   sl, ta       - beobachtete Step Lengths / Turning Angles (Radiant)
  #   sl_max       - Obergrenze des sl-Gitters
  #   n_bins_sl/ta - Anzahl Bins entlang der jeweiligen Achse
  #   ntree        - Anzahl Baeume im Random Forest
  #   sl_transform - "log1p": Bin-Grenzen gleich breit in der log1p(sl)-Skala.
  #                  Macht implizit die Annahme einer rechtsschiefen
  #                  sl-Verteilung (typisch fuer Bewegungsdaten, vgl. die
  #                  klassische Gamma-Verteilung fuer Step Lengths). Sehr
  #                  effektiv, wenn diese Annahme zutrifft.
  #                  "none": gleich breite Bins in der Original-sl-Skala
  #                  (einfachstes Verhalten - anfaellig fuer das eingangs
  #                  beschriebene Problem bei schiefen Verteilungen).
  #
  # Rueckgabe: ein randomForest-Objekt.
  fitDensitySurfaceRF <- function(sl, ta, sl_max,
                                  n_bins_sl = 30, n_bins_ta = 30,
                                  ntree = 500,
                                  sl_transform = c("log1p", "none")) {

    sl_transform <- match.arg(sl_transform)
    ta_breaks <- seq(-pi, pi, length.out = n_bins_ta + 1)
    ta_mid    <- (head(ta_breaks, -1) + tail(ta_breaks, -1)) / 2

    if (sl_transform == "log1p") {
      # --- log1p-Transformation: gleich breite Bins in der log1p(sl)-Skala ---
      # log1p(sl) = log(1 + sl): spreizt kleine sl-Unterschiede (z.B. 5m vs.
      # 20m), staucht grosse (z.B. 1000m vs. 1200m). Gleich breite Bins in
      # dieser Skala entsprechen damit ungleich breiten, aber inhaltlich
      # sinnvollen Bins im Original: schmal nahe 0, breit im Tail.
      sl_pred    <- log1p(sl)
      sl_max_pred <- log1p(sl_max)
      sl_breaks  <- seq(0, sl_max_pred, length.out = n_bins_sl + 1)
      sl_mid     <- (head(sl_breaks, -1) + tail(sl_breaks, -1)) / 2

      sl_bin <- cut(sl_pred, breaks = sl_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE)
      ta_bin <- cut(ta, breaks = ta_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE)
      count_table <- table(factor(sl_bin, levels = levels(sl_bin)),
                           factor(ta_bin, levels = levels(ta_bin)))

      # Bins sind in dieser (transformierten) Skala gleich breit -> rohe
      # Zaehldaten sind direkt proportional zur Dichte in dieser Skala.
      # Keine Division durch Bin-Breite notwendig.
      grid_df <- expand.grid(sl_pred = sl_mid, ta = ta_mid)
      grid_df$y <- as.vector(count_table)

    } else {
      # --- "none": gleich breite Bins in der Original-sl-Skala ---
      sl_breaks <- seq(0, sl_max, length.out = n_bins_sl + 1)
      sl_mid    <- (head(sl_breaks, -1) + tail(sl_breaks, -1)) / 2

      sl_bin <- cut(sl, breaks = sl_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE)
      ta_bin <- cut(ta, breaks = ta_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE)
      count_table <- table(factor(sl_bin, levels = levels(sl_bin)),
                           factor(ta_bin, levels = levels(ta_bin)))

      # Bins sind hier ebenfalls gleich breit (konstante Breite ueber den
      # gesamten sl-Bereich) -> rohe Zaehldaten sind direkt proportional zur
      # Dichte. Keine Division durch Bin-Breite notwendig.
      grid_df <- expand.grid(sl_pred = sl_mid, ta = ta_mid)
      grid_df$y <- as.vector(count_table)
    }

    # Random Forest fitten: y (Zaehldaten) ~ sl_pred + ta.
    rf_fit <- randomForest::randomForest(y ~ sl_pred + ta,
                                         data  = grid_df,
                                         ntree = ntree,
                                         mtry = 2)

    # Transformation als Attribut anhaengen, damit evalDensitySurfaceRF()
    # spaeter automatisch weiss, wie sl vor dem predict() behandelt werden
    # muss - ohne dass man sich das separat merken oder weiterreichen muss.
    attr(rf_fit, "sl_transform") <- sl_transform
    rf_fit
  }


  # Evaluate the (unnormalized) RF density surface at given points.
  #   sl, ta  - Punkte, an denen ausgewertet werden soll
  #   rf_fit  - randomForest-Objekt aus fitDensitySurfaceRF()
  # Rueckgabe: numeric vector mit vorhergesagten (unnormierten) Dichtewerten.
  evalDensitySurfaceRF <- function(sl, ta, rf_fit) {
    # sl_transform wurde beim Fitten als Attribut gespeichert (siehe
    # fitDensitySurfaceRF()) - dadurch muss man sich diese Information nicht
    # separat merken und an jede Stelle weiterreichen, an der das Modell
    # ausgewertet wird.
    sl_transform <- attr(rf_fit, "sl_transform")

    if (sl_transform == "log1p") {
      # Der RF wurde auf log1p(sl) trainiert -> dieselbe Transformation muss
      # vor dem predict() angewendet werden.
      sl_pred <- log1p(sl)
      pred <- stats::predict(rf_fit, newdata = data.frame(sl_pred = sl_pred, ta = ta))

      # JACOBIAN-KORREKTUR: Die RF-Vorhersage ist eine Dichte in der log1p(sl)-
      # Skala, nicht in der Original-sl-Skala. Beim Zuruecktransformieren
      # einer Dichte von einer Skala in eine andere muss man mit der
      # Ableitung der Transformation multiplizieren:
      #   d(log1p(sl))/d(sl) = 1 / (1 + sl)
      # Ohne diese Korrektur wuerde die Dichte im Tail (grosse sl)
      # systematisch ueberschaetzt.
      jacobian <- 1 / (1 + sl)
      dens <- pred * jacobian

    } else {
      # "none": der RF wurde direkt auf der Original-sl-Skala mit rohen
      # Zaehldaten als Zielvariable trainiert (siehe fitDensitySurfaceRF()) -
      # die Bins sind dort konstant breit, daher ist keine Rueck-
      # Transformation oder Jacobian-Korrektur notwendig.
      pred <- stats::predict(rf_fit, newdata = data.frame(sl_pred = sl, ta = ta))
      dens <- pred
    }

    # pmax(..., 0): numerische Rundungsfehler koennen winzige negative Werte
    # erzeugen, die wir hier auf 0 abschneiden (eine Dichte kann nicht negativ sein).
    pmax(dens, 0)
  }


  # Estimate the normalizing constant via Monte Carlo integration.
  #
  # predict() auf einem randomForest liefert keine echte Dichte (das Integral
  # ueber den gesamten Raum ist im Allgemeinen ungleich 1). Um daraus eine
  # gueltige Wahrscheinlichkeitsdichte zu machen, schaetzen wir das Integral
  # der Flaeche numerisch (Monte-Carlo-Integration) und teilen spaeter durch
  # diesen Wert.
  #
  # Idee: Integral ueber ein Rechteck = (Flaeche des Rechtecks) * (Mittelwert
  # der Funktion innerhalb des Rechtecks). Den Mittelwert schaetzen wir, indem
  # wir viele zufaellige Punkte gleichmaessig im Rechteck ziehen und dort die
  # Funktion auswerten.
  #
  #   rf_fit - randomForest-Objekt
  #   sl_max - Obergrenze des sl-Bereichs
  #   n_mc   - Anzahl der Monte-Carlo-Stichproben
  # Rueckgabe: numeric(1). Geschaetzte Normierungskonstante Z.
  estimateNormalizingConstantRF <- function(rf_fit, sl_max, n_mc = 20000) {
    mc_sl <- stats::runif(n_mc, 0, sl_max)
    mc_ta <- stats::runif(n_mc, -pi, pi)
    mc_vals <- evalDensitySurfaceRF(mc_sl, mc_ta, rf_fit)

    # Flaeche des Rechtecks [0, sl_max] x [-pi, pi]
    domain_area <- sl_max * 2 * pi

    mean(mc_vals) * domain_area
  }


  # Draw samples from the normalized RF surface via BayesianTools MCMC.
  #
  # Verwendet BayesianTools, um aus der (unnormierten) RF-Flaeche neue
  # (sl, ta)-Paare zu ziehen. BayesianTools erwartet eine Zielfunktion, die
  # eine LOG-Dichte zurueckgibt (nicht die Dichte selbst) - das ist Standard
  # bei MCMC-Verfahren, da log-Werte numerisch stabiler sind.
  #
  #   n          - gewuenschte Anzahl an Samples (nach Burn-in)
  #   rf_fit     - randomForest-Objekt
  #   sl_max     - Obergrenze des sl-Bereichs
  #   burn_in    - Anzahl der zu verwerfenden initialen Iterationen
  #   iterations - Gesamtzahl der MCMC-Iterationen; falls NULL, automatisch
  #                auf burn_in + n * 5 gesetzt
  #
  # Rueckgabe: eine Liste mit zwei Elementen:
  #   samples  - Matrix mit Spalten "sl" und "ta"
  #   mcmc_out - das vollstaendige BayesianTools-MCMC-Objekt, z.B. fuer
  #              BayesianTools::tracePlot() oder gelmanDiagnostics()
  bayesianToolsSampleDensitySurface <- function(n, rf_fit, sl_max,
                                                burn_in = 1000,
                                                iterations = NULL) {

    # Zielfunktion fuer BayesianTools: nimmt einen Parametervektor
    # par = c(sl, ta) entgegen und gibt einen einzelnen log-Dichtewert zurueck.
    log_density_fn <- function(par) {
      sl_val <- par[1]
      ta_val <- par[2]

      # Harte Grenzen: liegt der Vorschlag ausserhalb des gueltigen Bereichs,
      # ist die Wahrscheinlichkeit 0 -> log(0) = -Inf. BayesianTools lehnt
      # solche Vorschlaege dann automatisch ab.
      if (sl_val < 0 || sl_val > sl_max || ta_val < -pi || ta_val > pi) {
        return(-Inf)
      }

      dens <- evalDensitySurfaceRF(sl_val, ta_val, rf_fit)
      # + 1e-10 verhindert log(0) = -Inf an Stellen, wo der RF exakt 0 vorhersagt
      log(dens + 1e-10)
    }

    # createBayesianSetup() definiert das Optimierungs-/Sampling-Problem:
    # likelihood = unsere log-Dichte-Funktion, lower/upper = der Suchraum
    # (entspricht dem Definitionsbereich von sl und ta).
    bayesianSetup <- BayesianTools::createBayesianSetup(
      likelihood = log_density_fn,
      lower      = c(0, -pi),
      upper      = c(sl_max, pi)
    )

    if (is.null(iterations)) iterations <- burn_in + n * 5

    # sampler = "DEzs": Differential-Evolution-MCMC mit mehreren parallelen
    # Chains. Das ist robuster als ein einfaches Metropolis-Hastings, vor
    # allem weil Random-Forest-Vorhersagen stueckweise konstant sind (treppig)
    # und ein einfacher Sampler sich dort leicht "festfahren" kann.
    settings <- list(iterations = iterations, burnin = burn_in, message = FALSE)

    mcmc_out <- BayesianTools::runMCMC(bayesianSetup = bayesianSetup,
                                       sampler       = "DEzs",
                                       settings      = settings)

    # getSample() extrahiert die gezogenen Parameterwerte aus allen Chains,
    # der Burn-in-Bereich (start = burn_in + 1) wird dabei ausgeschlossen.
    samples_matrix <- BayesianTools::getSample(mcmc_out, start = burn_in + 1)
    colnames(samples_matrix) <- c("sl", "ta")

    # Falls mehr Samples vorhanden sind als benoetigt (n), zufaellig die
    # gewuenschte Anzahl auswaehlen.
    if (nrow(samples_matrix) > n) {
      keep <- sample(seq_len(nrow(samples_matrix)), n)
      samples_matrix <- samples_matrix[keep, , drop = FALSE]
    }

    # Falls WENIGER Samples vorhanden sind als benoetigt (n): BayesianTools'
    # DEzs-Sampler verwaltet Chains/Population-Groesse intern selbst, daher
    # entspricht die tatsaechliche Anzahl an Samples nach Abzug des Burn-in
    # nicht immer exakt "iterations - burn_in" - das passiert vor allem bei
    # kleinen angefragten n (z.B. n_control = 1). Wir gleichen das hier durch
    # Ziehen MIT Zuruecklegen (replace = TRUE) aus den vorhandenen Samples
    # aus, statt einen Fehler zu werfen. Das ist statistisch unproblematisch,
    # da die vorhandenen Samples bereits (nach Burn-in) aus der Zielverteilung
    # stammen - "mit Zuruecklegen ziehen" entspricht einem klassischen
    # Bootstrap und aendert die zugrunde liegende Verteilung nicht.
    if (nrow(samples_matrix) < n) {
      warning(
        "BayesianTools MCMC returned only ", nrow(samples_matrix),
        " samples after burn-in, but ", n, " were requested. ",
        "Filling the gap by resampling with replacement; consider increasing ",
        "`iterations` if this happens often.",
        call. = FALSE
      )
      extra_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(samples_matrix)),
                          size    = n - nrow(samples_matrix),
                          replace = TRUE)
      samples_matrix <- rbind(samples_matrix, samples_matrix[extra_idx, , drop = FALSE])
    }

    list(samples = samples_matrix, mcmc_out = mcmc_out)
  }


  # missing() muss VOR der naechsten Zeile (match.arg()) aufgerufen werden:
  # match.arg() bindet sl_transform neu (auf den ersten Default-Wert, falls
  # nichts uebergeben wurde), und danach laesst sich nicht mehr unterscheiden,
  # ob der Nutzer den Parameter explizit gesetzt hat oder der Default
  # einfach so "durchgereicht" wurde.
  sl_transform_was_set <- !missing(sl_transform)
  sl_transform <- match.arg(sl_transform)

  # --- Validierung (wie bisher) ---
  if (!inherits(x, c("steps_xy", "steps_xyt", "track_xy", "track_xyt"))) {
    stop("`x` must be an amt `steps_xy`, `steps_xyt`, `track_xy`, or `track_xyt` object.")}
  if (!is.numeric(n_control) || length(n_control) != 1L ||
      n_control != floor(n_control) || n_control < 1L) {
    stop("`n_control` must be a single positive integer.")}
  n_control <- as.integer(n_control)

  if (inherits(x, c("track_xy", "track_xyt")) &&
      !inherits(x, c("steps_xy", "steps_xyt"))) {
    x <- amt::steps(x)}
  x$step_id_ <- seq_len(nrow(x))
  estimator <- match.arg(estimator)

  # sl_transform wirkt nur im "density_advanced"-Zweig (siehe weiter unten).
  # Falls der Nutzer ihn trotzdem explizit gesetzt hat, aber einen anderen
  # estimator gewaehlt hat, wuerde der Parameter sonst stillschweigend
  # wirkungslos bleiben - das ist eine typische Quelle fuer "warum aendert
  # sich nichts?"-Verwirrung, deshalb hier eine explizite Warnung.
  if (sl_transform_was_set && estimator != "density_advanced") {
    warning(
      "`sl_transform` wird nur fuer `estimator = \"density_advanced\"` verwendet ",
      "und wird hier ignoriert, da `estimator = \"", estimator, "\"` gewaehlt wurde.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  # --- "traditional" (unveraendert) ---
  if (estimator == "traditional") {
    valid   <- !is.na(x$ta_) & !is.na(x$direction_p) & !is.na(x$sl_)
    x       <- x[valid, ]
    out     <- amt::random_steps(x, n_control = n_control)
    sl_fit  <- attr(out, "sl_")
    ta_fit  <- attr(out, "ta_")
    sl_prob <- stats::dgamma(out$sl_,
                             shape = sl_fit$params$shape,
                             scale = sl_fit$params$scale)
    ta_prob <- as.numeric(circular::dvonmises(
      circular::circular(out$ta_),
      mu    = ta_fit$params$mu,
      kappa = ta_fit$params$kappa))
    out$probability <- sl_prob * ta_prob
    class(out) <- c("random_steps_prop", class(out))
    return(out)}

  # Ab hier: "density" und "density_advanced" teilen sich die
  # Vorverarbeitung (gueltige Zeilen herausfiltern, sl_max bestimmen)
  valid   <- !is.na(x$ta_) & !is.na(x$direction_p) & !is.na(x$sl_)
  x_valid <- x[valid, ]
  sl_max  <- max(x_valid$sl_) * 1.5
  n_obs   <- nrow(x_valid)

  # --- "density" (KDE, unveraendert) ---
  if (estimator == "density") {

    obs_movement <- cbind(sl = x_valid$sl_, ta = x_valid$ta_)
    H_hat   <- ks::Hpi(obs_movement)
    kde_fit <- ks::kde(obs_movement, H = H_hat, xmin = c(0, -pi), xmax = c(sl_max, pi))

    draw_kde <- function(n, kde_obj) {
      candidates <- ks::rkde(n * 2, fhat = kde_obj)
      keep <- candidates[candidates[, "sl"] > 0 &
                           candidates[, "ta"] >= -pi &
                           candidates[, "ta"] <= pi, , drop = FALSE]
      if (nrow(keep) < n) stop("Too many drawn samples out of range.")
      keep[seq_len(n), ]
    }

    n_total      <- n_obs * n_control
    random_draws <- draw_kde(n_total, kde_fit)
    sl_random    <- random_draws[, "sl"]
    ta_random    <- random_draws[, "ta"]

    obs_idx <- rep(seq_len(n_obs), each = n_control)
    abs_angle <- x_valid$direction_p[obs_idx] + ta_random
    x2_random <- x_valid$x1_[obs_idx] + sl_random * cos(abs_angle)
    y2_random <- x_valid$y1_[obs_idx] + sl_random * sin(abs_angle)

    random_tbl <- x_valid[obs_idx, ]
    random_tbl$x2_ <- x2_random
    random_tbl$y2_ <- y2_random
    random_tbl$sl_ <- sl_random
    random_tbl$ta_ <- ta_random
    random_tbl$case_ <- FALSE
    random_tbl$step_id_ <- rep(x_valid$step_id_, each = n_control)
    random_tbl$probability <- stats::predict(kde_fit, x = cbind(sl_random, ta_random))

    obs_tbl <- x_valid
    obs_tbl$case_ <- TRUE
    obs_tbl$probability <- stats::predict(kde_fit, x = cbind(x_valid$sl_, x_valid$ta_))

    core_cols <- c("step_id_", "case_", "probability", "x1_", "x2_", "y1_", "y2_", "sl_", "ta_")
    time_cols <- intersect(c("t1_", "t2_", "dt_"), names(x_valid))
    keep_cols <- c(core_cols, time_cols)

    out <- rbind(obs_tbl[, keep_cols], random_tbl[, keep_cols])
    out <- out[order(out$step_id_, !out$case_), ]

    base_steps_class <- if (inherits(x, "steps_xyt")) "steps_xyt" else "steps_xy"
    class(out) <- c(
      "random_steps_prop",
      "random_steps",
      base_steps_class,
      setdiff(class(out), c("random_steps_prop", "random_steps",
                            "steps_xyt", "steps_xy"))
    )
    return(out)
  }

  # --- "density_advanced" (Random Forest + BayesianTools) ---
  if (estimator == "density_advanced") {

    # 1. Glatte (bzw. hier: stueckweise konstante) Dichte-Landschaft fitten
    rf_fit <- fitDensitySurfaceRF(x_valid$sl_, x_valid$ta_, sl_max,
                                  n_bins_sl    = rf_n_bins,
                                  n_bins_ta    = rf_n_bins,
                                  ntree        = rf_ntree,
                                  sl_transform = sl_transform)

    # 2. Normierungskonstante schaetzen (Integral der Flaeche = 1 erzwingen)
    Z <- estimateNormalizingConstantRF(rf_fit, sl_max)

    # 3. Random Steps aus der normierten Flaeche samplen
    n_total <- n_obs * n_control
    mh_result <- bayesianToolsSampleDensitySurface(n_total, rf_fit, sl_max,
                                                   burn_in = mcmc_burn_in)
    sl_random <- mh_result$samples[, "sl"]
    ta_random <- mh_result$samples[, "ta"]

    # 4. Endkoordinaten rekonstruieren (analog zu den anderen Branches)
    obs_idx <- rep(seq_len(n_obs), each = n_control)
    abs_angle <- x_valid$direction_p[obs_idx] + ta_random
    x2_random <- x_valid$x1_[obs_idx] + sl_random * cos(abs_angle)
    y2_random <- x_valid$y1_[obs_idx] + sl_random * sin(abs_angle)

    random_tbl <- x_valid[obs_idx, ]
    random_tbl$x2_ <- x2_random
    random_tbl$y2_ <- y2_random
    random_tbl$sl_ <- sl_random
    random_tbl$ta_ <- ta_random
    random_tbl$case_ <- FALSE
    random_tbl$step_id_ <- rep(x_valid$step_id_, each = n_control)
    random_tbl$probability <- evalDensitySurfaceRF(sl_random, ta_random, rf_fit) / Z

    obs_tbl <- x_valid
    obs_tbl$case_ <- TRUE
    obs_tbl$probability <- evalDensitySurfaceRF(x_valid$sl_, x_valid$ta_, rf_fit) / Z

    core_cols <- c("step_id_", "case_", "probability", "x1_", "x2_", "y1_", "y2_", "sl_", "ta_")
    time_cols <- intersect(c("t1_", "t2_", "dt_"), names(x_valid))
    keep_cols <- c(core_cols, time_cols)

    out <- rbind(obs_tbl[, keep_cols], random_tbl[, keep_cols])
    out <- out[order(out$step_id_, !out$case_), ]

    base_steps_class <- if (inherits(x, "steps_xyt")) "steps_xyt" else "steps_xy"
    class(out) <- c(
      "random_steps_prop",
      "random_steps",
      base_steps_class,
      setdiff(class(out), c("random_steps_prop", "random_steps",
                            "steps_xyt", "steps_xy"))
    )

    # MCMC-Objekt als Attribut anhaengen, damit man spaeter Diagnostik
    # (Trace-Plots, Gelman-Rubin) durchfuehren kann, ohne die Funktion
    # erneut aufrufen zu muessen.
    attr(out, "mcmc_out") <- mh_result$mcmc_out

    return(out)
  }
}
```

## `extractStepCovariates()`

**Description.** Extracts habitat covariate values at the coordinates of each step (observed and random) in a `random_steps_prop` object, for use with `dnn_ssf()`. For numeric layers, values are extracted directly at the step endpoint (`x2_`, `y2_`). For image layers, kernel-aggregated values are computed over a square neighbourhood around the endpoint (e.g. a local mean), rather than at a single pixel. Column names are taken from the layer names of each `SpatRaster`. Coordinates that fall outside a layer's extent are set to `NA` and a warning is issued.

**Arguments.**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | A `random_steps_prop` (or `steps_covariates`) object, as returned by `createRandomSteps()`. |
| `numericLayers` | `SpatRasterCollection` of numeric/binary covariate layers, or `NULL`. |
| `imageLayers` | `SpatRasterCollection` of image-like covariate layers, or `NULL`. |
| `imageKernelDimensions`, `imageKernelFunctions` | Kernel size and aggregation function per image layer. |
| `scaleNumericLayers`, `scaleImageLayers` | Whether to rescale layers to (0, 1) before extraction. |

**Value.** An object of class `steps_covariates` (extending the class of `x`) with one additional column per layer, named after the corresponding `SpatRaster`.

```{r extractStepCovariates-source, eval = FALSE}
extractStepCovariates <- function(x,
                                  numericLayers         = NULL,
                                  imageLayers           = NULL,
                                  imageKernelDimensions = c(3),
                                  imageKernelFunctions  = list(f1 = mean),
                                  scaleNumericLayers    = TRUE,
                                  scaleImageLayers      = TRUE) {

# Internal helper functions ---------------------------------------------
# cropScaleRaster() and extractKernelValues() are also used by
# simulateTrack() (see simulation.R), but since local/nested functions are
# not visible outside the function they are defined in, they are defined
# again here as local copies - together with checkExtent(), which is only
# ever needed inside extractStepCovariates().

  # Crops a raster layer to a given extent and optionally rescales it to (0, 1).
  #   layer - SpatRaster to process
  #   ext   - SpatExtent to crop to
  #   scale - if TRUE, rescale cropped values to (0, 1); skipped if the layer
  #           is constant (min == max), since dividing by zero would occur
  cropScaleRaster <- function(layer, ext, scale = TRUE) {
    r <- terra::crop(layer, ext)
    terra::ext(r) <- ext
    if (scale) {
      r_min <- terra::global(r, "min", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
      r_max <- terra::global(r, "max", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
      if (r_max > r_min) r <- (r - r_min) / (r_max - r_min)
    }
    r
  }

  # For each coordinate pair (xs[i], ys[i]), extracts the raster values inside
  # a square window of kernelDim x kernelDim pixels centred on that point and
  # aggregates them with kernelFun (e.g. mean, max). Raster borders are
  # wrapped toroidally, i.e. a window that runs off one edge of the raster
  # continues on the opposite edge.
  #   raster    - SpatRaster to read from
  #   xs, ys    - coordinates of the query points (same length)
  #   kernelDim - odd side length (in pixels) of the square window
  #   kernelFun - aggregation function applied to the values in each window
  extractKernelValues <- function(raster, xs, ys, kernelDim, kernelFun) {
    res_x <- terra::res(raster)[1]
    res_y <- terra::res(raster)[2]
    half  <- floor(kernelDim / 2)

    border  <- terra::ext(raster)
    x_range <- border[2] - border[1]
    y_range <- border[4] - border[3]

    offsets <- expand.grid(dx = seq(-half, half),
                           dy = seq(-half, half))
    n_pts <- length(xs)
    n_off <- nrow(offsets)

    all_x <- rep(xs, each = n_off) +
      rep(offsets$dx, times = n_pts) * res_x
    all_y <- rep(ys, each = n_off) +
      rep(offsets$dy, times = n_pts) * res_y

    all_x <- ((all_x - border[1]) %% x_range) + border[1]
    all_y <- ((all_y - border[3]) %% y_range) + border[3]

    vals_all <- terra::extract(raster, cbind(all_x, all_y))[, 1]
    vals_mat <- matrix(vals_all, nrow = n_pts,
                       ncol = n_off, byrow = TRUE)

    apply(vals_mat, 1, function(row) {
      v <- row[!is.na(row)]
      if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else kernelFun(v)
    })
  }

  # Warns if any coordinates lie outside the extent of a given raster layer.
  #   xs, ys - coordinates to check
  #   raster - SpatRaster whose extent is checked against
  # Rueckgabe: logical vector, TRUE where the coordinate lies outside.
  checkExtent <- function(xs, ys, raster) {
    ext      <- terra::ext(raster)
    lyr_name <- names(raster)
    outside  <- xs < ext[1] | xs > ext[2] | ys < ext[3] | ys > ext[4]
    if (any(outside, na.rm = TRUE))
      warning(sum(outside, na.rm = TRUE),
              " coordinate(s) out of layer '", lyr_name, "' extent; set to NA.",
              call. = FALSE)
    outside}


  # Validation:

  if (!inherits(x, c("random_steps_prop","steps_covariates") ))
    stop("`x` must be an object of class 'random_steps_prop' or 'steps_covariates'.")
  if (is.null(numericLayers) && is.null(imageLayers))
    stop("At least one of `numericLayers` or `imageLayers` must be provided.")
  if (!is.null(numericLayers)) {
    if (!inherits(numericLayers, "SpatRasterCollection"))
      stop("`numericLayers` must be of class 'SpatRasterCollection'.")}
  if (!is.null(imageLayers)) {
    if (!inherits(imageLayers, "SpatRasterCollection"))
      stop("`imageLayers` must be of class 'SpatRasterCollection'.")
    nImage <- length(terra::as.list(imageLayers))
    if (length(imageKernelDimensions) != nImage)
      stop("`imageKernelDimensions` must have one entry per image layer.")
    if (length(imageKernelFunctions) != nImage)
      stop("`imageKernelFunctions` must have one entry per image layer.")
    if (any(imageKernelDimensions %% 2 == 0))
      stop("All `imageKernelDimensions` must be odd numbers.")}

  # CRS check
  rasterList <- c(
    if (!is.null(numericLayers)) terra::as.list(numericLayers) else list(),
    if (!is.null(imageLayers))   terra::as.list(imageLayers)   else list())
  if (length(rasterList) > 1) {
    crsList  <- sapply(rasterList, terra::crs)
    nonEmpty <- crsList[nchar(crsList) > 0]
    if (length(nonEmpty) > 1 && length(unique(nonEmpty)) > 1)
      stop("All layers must have the same CRS.")}


  xs <- x$x2_
  ys <- x$y2_


  # Extract numeric layer values:

  if (!is.null(numericLayers)) {
    numericRasterList <- terra::as.list(numericLayers)

    for (k in seq_along(numericRasterList)) {
      r        <- cropScaleRaster(numericRasterList[[k]],
                                  ext   = terra::ext(numericRasterList[[k]]),
                                  scale = scaleNumericLayers)
      lyr_name <- names(r)
      outside  <- checkExtent(xs, ys, r)
      vals     <- terra::extract(r, cbind(xs, ys))[, 1]
      vals[outside] <- NA_real_
      x[[lyr_name]] <- vals
    }
  }


  # Extract image layer kernel values

  if (!is.null(imageLayers)) {
    imageRasterList <- terra::as.list(imageLayers)

    for (k in seq_along(imageRasterList)) {
      r        <- cropScaleRaster(imageRasterList[[k]],
                                  ext   = terra::ext(imageRasterList[[k]]),
                                  scale = scaleImageLayers)
      lyr_name <- names(r)
      outside  <- checkExtent(xs, ys, r)

      vals           <- rep(NA_real_, length(xs))
      inside_idx     <- which(!outside)
      if (length(inside_idx) > 0) {
        vals[inside_idx] <- extractKernelValues(
          raster    = r,
          xs        = xs[inside_idx],
          ys        = ys[inside_idx],
          kernelDim = imageKernelDimensions[k],
          kernelFun = imageKernelFunctions[[k]]
        )
      }
      x[[lyr_name]] <- vals
    }
  }


  # New class

  class(x) <- c("steps_covariates", setdiff(class(x), "steps_covariates"))
  x
}
```

## `extractStepImagekernels()`

**Description.** Extracts raw image kernels around the coordinates of each step in a `random_steps_prop` object, for use with `cnn_ssf()`. Images are provided as one or multiple `.tif` files (e.g. orthophoto tiles), which are combined into a single virtual mosaic via `terra::vrt()`. For each step endpoint, a square kernel of the requested radius is cropped from the mosaic across all image bands and min-max scaled (either to a user-supplied range, e.g. `c(0, 255)` for 8-bit imagery, or to the global observed range). The result is stored as one list-column containing, for each step, a 3D array of dimension `[nrow, ncol, n_bands]` - the format expected as CNN input by `cnn_ssf()`.

**Arguments.**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `x` | A `random_steps_prop` (or `steps_covariates`) object, as returned by `createRandomSteps()`. |
| `tifDirectory` | Path to a folder containing one or multiple `.tif` files. |
| `kernelRadius` | Radius (in meters) of the square kernel extracted around each step endpoint. |
| `imageScaling` | Optional known value range (e.g. `c(0, 255)`) used to rescale pixel values; if `NULL`, the global min/max of the mosaic is used. |
| `colName` | Name of the new list-column; defaults to the folder name of `tifDirectory`. |

**Value.** An object of class `steps_covariates` (extending the class of `x`) with one additional list-column of 3D image-kernel arrays, one array per step.

```{r extractStepImagekernels-source, eval = FALSE}
extractStepImagekernels <- function(x,
                                    tifDirectory = NULL,
                                    kernelRadius = NULL,
                                    imageScaling = NULL,
                                    colName      = NULL) {

  # Validation

  if (!inherits(x, c("random_steps_prop", "steps_covariates")))
    stop("`x` must be an object of class 'random_steps_prop' or 'steps_covariates'.")
  if (!dir.exists(tifDirectory))
    stop("Directory does not exist: ", tifDirectory)
  if (is.null(kernelRadius))
    stop("`kernelRadius` must be provided.")
  if (!is.numeric(kernelRadius) || length(kernelRadius) != 1)
    stop("`kernelRadius` must be a single numeric value.")
  if (kernelRadius <= 0)
    stop("`kernelRadius` must be a positive number.")
  if (!is.null(imageScaling)) {
    if (!is.numeric(imageScaling) || length(imageScaling) != 2)
      stop("`imageScaling` must be a numeric vector of length 2, e.g. c(0, 255).")
    if (imageScaling[1] >= imageScaling[2])
      stop("`imageScaling[1]` must be smaller than `imageScaling[2]`.")
  }
  if (!is.null(colName) && (!is.character(colName) || length(colName) != 1))
    stop("`colName` must be a single character string.")

  # Building virtual mosaic out of all .tif data with terra::vrt()

  tif_files <- list.files(tifDirectory, pattern = "\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(tif_files) == 0) stop("No .tif files in: ", tifDirectory)

  vrt_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".vrt")
  r        <- terra::vrt(tif_files, filename = vrt_path, overwrite = TRUE)
  n_bands  <- terra::nlyr(r)

  # Column name: user-provided or derived from folder name
  if (is.null(colName)) {
    colName <- basename(normalizePath(tifDirectory, mustWork = FALSE))
  }

  # CRS check
  if (is.na(terra::crs(r)) || terra::crs(r) == "")
    warning("Raster has no defined CRS. Make sure coordinates and images share the same projection.")

  # Coordinates as SpatVector
  pts <- terra::vect(as.data.frame(x), geom = c("x2_", "y2_"), crs = terra::crs(r))

  # Check if steps lie outside the raster coverage
  mosaic_ext <- terra::ext(r)
  xs <- x$x2_
  ys <- x$y2_

  outside <- xs < mosaic_ext[1] | xs > mosaic_ext[2] |
    ys < mosaic_ext[3] | ys > mosaic_ext[4]

  if (any(outside)) {
    warning(
      "Step(s) ", paste(which(outside), collapse = ", "),
      " lie outside the raster coverage; image band values set to NA.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  # Determine band min/max for normalization
  if (!is.null(imageScaling)) {
    band_min <- rep(imageScaling[1], n_bands)
    band_max <- rep(imageScaling[2], n_bands)
  } else {
    band_range <- terra::global(r, fun = "range", na.rm = TRUE)
    band_min   <- band_range[, "min"]
    band_max   <- band_range[, "max"]
  }

  # Preparing list for image kernels
  kernel_list <- vector("list", nrow(x))

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(x))) {

    if (outside[i]) {
      kernel_list[[i]] <- list(NULL)
      next
    }

    pt <- pts[i, ]
    e  <- terra::ext(
      terra::crds(pt)[1] - kernelRadius, terra::crds(pt)[1] + kernelRadius,
      terra::crds(pt)[2] - kernelRadius, terra::crds(pt)[2] + kernelRadius
    )

    kernel <- terra::crop(r, e, snap = "near")

    if (terra::nrow(kernel) == 0 || terra::ncol(kernel) == 0 ||
        terra::nlyr(kernel) != n_bands) {
      warning("Step ", i, ": kernel could not be extracted; values set to NA.",
              call. = FALSE)
      kernel_list[[i]] <- list(NULL)
    } else {
      kernel_list[[i]] <- kernel
    }
  }

  # Adding kernels as one column with 3D array [nrow, ncol, n_bands]
  x[[colName]] <- lapply(kernel_list, function(k) {
    if (is.null(k)) return(NA)

    nr       <- terra::nrow(k)
    nc       <- terra::ncol(k)
    combined <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(nr, nc, n_bands))

    arr_3d <- terra::as.array(k)                    # <-- einmal, für alle Bänder
    for (b_idx in seq_len(n_bands)) {
      combined[, , b_idx] <- (arr_3d[, , b_idx] - band_min[b_idx]) /
        (band_max[b_idx] - band_min[b_idx])
    }

    combined
  })

  class(x) <- c("steps_covariates", class(x))
  return(x)
}
```
